quote: For an early "Backrooms" game, it nails the atmosphere. It was great to explore this famous liminal space.

author: futureblues
quote:
I thoroughly enjoyed Silent Hill: Townfall. The atmosphere is oppressive and beautiful. The brutalist architecture is menacing and a wonder to explore.

This is a great stealth, survival horror experience. The creatures are appropriately imposing. It could've used two or three more creature designs, in my opinion, but beyond that I have no major complaints.

author: futureblues
quote:
There have been no meaningful innovations to the "real life sim" genre since GTA III. This game continues the trend of treading water. Yes, the graphics are more realistic, but the gameplay is the same.

On top of that, the game uncritically promotes contemporary transphobia.

author: futureblues
quote:
This is an amazing game. A masterclass in atmosphere, with fantastic music and storytelling. It's filled with fun puzzles and exciting boss fights against a menagerie of unique demons.

I'd give the game a 10, but it crashes during survival mode on PS5.

2XKO was known for crisp visuals, but unremarkable gameplay. I'd only recommend the most fervent of fighting game fans check it out.

author: futureblues
quote:
An incredibly focused and confident game.
It makes traversing a rocky, mountainous continent an engrossing experience. It's fetch quests / delivery jobs refined to perfection.
The story plays with the current isolation crisis, with our psychological seclusion represented with literal isolated bunkers. It floats many fun theories on the nature of human connection, constantly giving you new perspectives to chew on.
And if that sounds too heady, remember you can always go slam energy drinks while rocking out to Bring Me the Horizon in any of Sam's private rooms!

author: futureblues
quote: Amazing experience. It pulls you into a dark, exciting world that is oppressive enough to keep you wondering what might be lurking in the shadows and intriguing enough to keep you champing at the bit for insight into how it became the way it is.

author: futureblues
quote:
Don't waste your time with this one.
The game presents itself as a thoughtful exploration of depression, which would be admirable if that was true. It, at best, superficially presents the complex mental disorder. Wearing "depression" as an eye-catching label to market the game, rather than paying respect to individuals who suffer from depression, feels gross to me.

author: futureblues
quote:
Fantastic entry in the Resident Evil series. The game is stuffed with homages to previous RE games without pandering or feeling repetitive.

Grace is a wonderful new character, bringing a relatable anxiety to RE's world of callous elites and engineered monstrosities.

author: futureblues

author: futureblues
quote:
Fantastic atmosphere and graphics. The European setting is very well realized and feels great to explore.
The RPG gameplay is functional, not bad but not above average.
The problem comes from the writing. Koudelka, the protagonist, is beyond unlikable. She's written as a cooler-than-you Joss Whedon wet dream. In other words, she's insufferable.
With better writing this could be a real gem, but as it is the only way to play is on mute, skipping all dialogue and cutscenes.

author: futureblues
quote:
Steel Wool did a fantastic job.  This game is a blast.  The mega pizzaplex is a great mix of realistic yet greatly, greatly exaggerated (as a child would see a mega playground pizza place).  It introduces a ton of memorable new characters.  It continues the FNaF tradition of including fun, bonus minigames.

I got all the trophies for the game, and I'm still itching to jump back into its world.  Cheers to Steel Wool.  Thanks for the good times.

author: futureblues
quote:
A fun survival scenario, that is very well realized.

It's a simple concept, in a game with a simple gameplay loop. You are a night security guard at a kids' pizza place with a handful of mascot animatronics. The animatronics will move and try to reach you. You can monitor them on a feed of the restaurant's cameras and can manually close your office doors to protect yourself. These actions use up power, though, and you only have a finite amount of juice to last you the night.

This first entry in the FNaF series is, in my opinion, still the best at creating horror. The animatronics have never looked better, by looking the most like something a real-world amusement attraction could conceivably own. I've never seen a real-life animatronic that didn't look abjectly terrifying, so the more FNaF models prioritize looking realistic, the better. Other entries in the series may be more effective at creating tension, but tension and horror are very different beasts and I believe FNaF 1 is the best horror game in the series.

author: futureblues
quote:
A terrific 1v1 FNaF experience.

I love how this entry switched-up the FNaF formula to host a unique player vs one threat (Springtrap) scenario. Both contestants have handicaps to keep the night tense and engaging.
Springtrap wants to head right to your office, but is beholden to the programing in its circuitry. if you play audio of children near Springtrap, it's impelled to head for the children who, it believes, need to be entertained.
You have the above mentioned audio lures along with a monitor of camera feeds covering most places Springtrap will be. Your equipment can fall into malfunction states, becoming unresponsive. It takes precious time to reboot your systems, giving Springtrap opportunity to get an edge.

I love the haunted house atmosphere of the game. The cat and mouse style gameplay is a fantastic iteration of the core FNaF survival formula. Recommended for people interested the FNaF games and people looking for a breezy, engaging horror experience.

author: futureblues
quote:
I really like the concept of a core-series FNaF game being more story focused. Baby is a great new character, who brings a lot of juicy lore with her.  The graphics are fantastic.

My complaints are with the gameplay.  I can't think of a single minigame from SL that I would want to go back to later to re-experience. On the other hand, I think the classic-FNaF survival section in SL is the most aggravating and unbalanced of the main games. 3 minutes of slow tedium followed by 3 minutes of a far too aggressive AI, that (I can't prove this) seems to have a RNG check that starts around 4am that gives a decent chance of a random, unavoidable death.
game_title: Five Nights at Freddy's: Sister Location
